questions.stem: A patient admitted to ICU with AMI suffers a second attack on the fourth day. Which of the following is the best marker/test to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Serial values of Troponin T/I
  • The laboratory evaluation of MI is based on measuring blood levels of macromolecules that leak out of injured myocardial cells through damaged cell membranes.
  • These molecules include myoglobin, cardiac troponins T and I (TnT, TnI), creatine kinase (CK; specifically, the myocardial isoform, CK-MB), and lactate dehydrogenase.
  • Troponins (and to a lesser extent CK-MB) have high specificity and sensitivity for myocardial damage.
  • TnI and TnT normally are not found in the circulation; however, after acute MI, both are detectable within 2 to 4 hours, with levels peaking at 48 hours and remaining elevated for 7 to 10 days. Persistence of elevated troponin levels allows the diagnosis of an acute MI to be made long after CK-MB levels have returned to normal. With reperfusion, both troponin and CK-MB levels may peak earlier owing to a more rapid washout of the enzyme from the necrotic tissue.
  • Option B. CK-MB has long been the biomarker of myocardial injury but is now tested less frequently in favor of the more sensitive cardiac-specific troponins. Total CK activity is not a reliable marker of cardiac injury since various isoforms of CK are found in non-cardiac tissues. However, the CK-MB isoform—principally derived from the myocardium, but also present at low levels in skeletal muscle—is a more specific indicator of heart damage. CK-MB activity begins to rise within 2 to 4 hours of MI, peaks at 24 to 48 hours, and returns to normal within approximately 72 hours



Robbins Basic pathology, 10th Edition, Page No. 417

questions.stem: Isoenzymes in the form of biomarkers are useful in the diagnosis of tissue damage and other diseases. Which is the predominant isoenzyme of LDH released in liver injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
LDH - 5
  • In the Liver, both LDH-4 & 5 are present but LDH-5 isoenzyme is the major form (Option C is excluded). So, in liver injury, LDH-5 will be predominantly released).
  • LDH-5 is also a marker for radio sensitization
  • In muscles also, both LDH-4 & LDH-5 are present but the LDH-5 isoenzyme is predominant. Increased LDH-5 in serum is a marker for muscular dystrophy.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition page. 67

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: Trypsinogen, a protease present in pancreatic secretion is an inactive form of the enzyme trypsin. Which of the following process will activate trypsinogen to its active form trypsin?

options.label: D
options.text: Removal of part of the protein

questions.answerText: Removal of part of the protein
questions.solutionHtml:
Removal of part of the protein
  • Many enzymes (mainly digestive enzymes) are first synthesized as inactive precursors, known as Zymogens or Proenzymes.
  • In a zymogen, part of the protein blocks the active site of the enzyme. Cleaving off this peptide activates the enzyme.
  • For example, trypsinogen to trypsin activation requires the removal of the first 15 amino acid residues from the N-terminal end which is done by enteropeptidase present in the intestinal mucosa.
  • Trypsinogen → Trypsin + peptide fragment
  • Activated trypsin thus produced can cleave more trypsinogen to its active form. This is known as autocatalytic activation.



Lippincott Illustrated Reviews Biochemistry. 7th edition page. 175

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: One of the methods of regulation of an enzyme's or a protein's activity is the phosphorylation of some of its amino acid residues. Which of the following statement is false about this covalent modification?

options.label: B
options.text: It is slower than allosteric regulation

options.label: C
options.text: It uses the same enzyme for activation and inactivation

options.label: D
options.text: Phosphorylation is a common covalent modification

questions.answerText: It uses the same enzyme for activation and inactivation
questions.solutionHtml:
It uses the same enzyme for activation and inactivation

Phosphorylation of protein:

  • It is considered the most common covalent modification (Option D is true).
  • Phosphorylation of protein is done for activating or inactivating an enzyme. This method of regulation uses separate enzymes for activation and inactivation (Option C is false).
    • The enzyme which adds phosphate is the protein kinase
    • The enzyme which removes phosphate is protein phosphatase.
  • It is a covalent modification that is mediated by hormonal action such as insulin and glucagon.
  • The hormonal release and signaling is a time taking process, so, phosphorylation can be regarded as a slow and long-term regulation compared to allosteric regulation of the enzyme which is usually done instantaneously in the cell mostly by substrate or product of reaction (Option B is true).
  • It is reversible as, with the removal of the signal or presence of an antagonistic hormone, the condition of the enzyme can be reversed (Option A is true).
  • Oher covalent modifications are:
    • Adenylation, uridylation
    • ADP ribosylation
    • methylation
    • acetylation



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 90-92

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: Which statement is false about allosteric regulation?

options.label: A
options.text: It is usually the mode of regulation of the last step in reaction pathways

options.label: B
options.text: Cellular response is rapid with allosteric control than by controlling enzyme concentration in the cell

options.label: C
options.text: The regulation usually is important for the conservation of energy and materials in cells

options.label: D
options.text: Allosteric modulators bind non-covalently at sites other than the active site and induce conformational changes in the enzyme

questions.answerText: It is usually the mode of regulation of the last step in reaction pathways
questions.solutionHtml:
It is usually the mode of regulation of the last step in reaction pathways
  • Allosteric regulation is usually the mode of regulation operating at the first step in the reaction pathway. This is nature’s way to minimize the wastage of energy and resources spent on carrying out subsequent steps of the pathways (option C is true).


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 88

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: Most proteins in the cells are under continuous turnover by a well-designed cycle of synthesis and degradation. The mechanism of degradation of defective proteins involves their covalent attachment to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ubiquitin
  • The Ubiquitin-Proteasome Pathway (UPP) is the main & highly regulated mechanism for protein degradation. It uses ATP.
  • Ubiquitin protein:
    • It is present in the cytoplasm and nucleus.
    • It is a highly conserved, small, globular, non-enzymic protein and is recycled.
    • It is used as part of the UPP pathway to degrade damaged, short-lived or misfolded proteins.
    • ε-amino of lysine in protein gets attached with a covalent bond to C-terminal glycine of ubiquitin by an isopeptide bond.

Mechanism of working of the Ubiquitin-Proteasome pathway





Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 87-88

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: In thyroid hormone production, thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) from the hypothalamus stimulates thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) release from the anterior pituitary, which stimulates the thyroid to produce thyroid hormones (triiodothyronine [T3] and thyroxine [T4]). Normal or high levels of thyroid hormone then suppress the release of TRH. The regulation of this pathway is best described by which one of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Feedback regulation

In feedback regulation, the end-product (thyroid hormones) directly controls its rate of synthesis by suppressing earlier stimulating hormones. This is called a feedback loop.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 87-88

questions.stemHtml: Which LDH isoenzyme has maximum electrophoretic mobility:
questions.solutionHtml:
LDH-1
  • Isoenzymes differ in their amino acid sequences which creates a difference in their charges and molecular weights.
  • This difference is used for their separation using the gel electrophoresis technique.
  • Electrophoretic mobility differs among the LDH isoenzymes so they can be separated in an electrophoretic setup.
  • Based on the electrophoretic mobility, always number ‘1’ is given to the isozyme form having maximum electrophoretic mobility, and the last number is given to the form with the least mobility.
  • LDH-1 (Option A) and CK-1 have maximum electrophoretic mobility whereas LDH-5 (Option B) and CK-3 have the least electrophoretic mobility.
  • All other isoforms LDH-2 (Option C), LDH-3 (Option D), and LDH-4 are in between.
  • As LDH-2 has maximum concentration in blood, that's why its peak is highest.




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 67

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: A 50-year-old alcoholic had passed out in a street after heavy drinking. When his family members found him, he was rushed to the emergency department. The physician gave him an injection of thiamine followed by overnight parenteral glucose. The patient was alert and coherent the next morning, with normal serum thiamine and his blood glucose was 73 mg/dL (4 mM). He was discharged from the hospital soon after. Which of the following enzymes/proteins would have no significant physiologic activity in this patient soon after discharge?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucokinase
  • After an overnight fast (plasma glucose 73 mg/dL), the glucose concentration will be low.
  • At low glucose levels, hexokinase with its higher afﬁnity for glucose can convert all the glucose to glucose 6-phosphate without triggering the release of its isozyme for glucokinase hence glucokinase concentration remains low.
  • Glucokinase has a higher Michaelis-Menten constant (Km) than hexokinase, so, it is most active in postprandial state when glucose levels are high in the liver.
  • So, in this patient, the activity of glucokinase would be insignificant as it requires high glucose concentration to be effective.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 144, 166

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the ubiquitin proteasomal system are true/false?A. Intracellular, short-lived regulatory proteins are degradedB. Non α peptide bond is formed by ubiquitinC. α peptide bond is formed by ubiquitinD. Amino-terminal Asp or Arg accelerate ubiquitinationE. ATP independentSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
T, T, F, T, F
  • The Ubiquitin-Proteasome Pathway (UPP) is the main & highly regulated mechanism for protein degradation. It uses ATP (Option E is False).
  • Ubiquitin protein:
  • It is present in the cytoplasm and nucleus.
  • It is a highly conserved, small, globular, non-enzymic protein and is recycled.
  • It is used as part of the UPP pathway to degrade damaged, misfolded proteins and short-lived proteins e.g. intracellular Protein, and regulatory Protein (Option A is true).
  • ε-amino of lysine in protein gets attached with a covalent bond to C-terminal glycine of ubiquitin by an isopeptide bond which is a non-alpha peptide bond (Option B is true, and C is false).
  • The proteins having amino acids (Arginine, Acetylated alanine, Aspartate) at the N-terminal end are rapidly degraded or have short half-lives. This is known as the N-end rule. A residue present at the amino terminus of a protein determines whether a protein is ubiquitinated or not N-terminal Met or Ser residues retard, whereas N-terminal Asp or Arg accelerate ubiquitination (Option D is true).
Mechanism of working of the Ubiquitin-Proteasome pathway



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 280-281

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: Which of the following can occur in the covalent modification of enzymes?a. Dephosphorylationb. Phosphorylationc. Proteolytic cleavaged. Activation by divalent cationSelect the correct answer from the given below code:

options.label: B
options.text: If a and d are correct

options.label: C
options.text: If a, b, and c are correct

options.label: D
options.text: If all four (a, b, c, & d) are correct

questions.answerText: If a, b, and c are correct
questions.solutionHtml:
If a, b, and c are correct
  • Divalent cations are cofactors for the enzymes (not a covalent modification)
  • Enzyme activity can be modulated by the post-translational covalent modification of an enzyme.
  • The most common covalent modification is phosphorylation & dephosphorylation.
  • Other covalent modifications are:-
    • Adenylation
    • Uridylation
    • ADP Ribosylation
    • Methylation
    • Acetylation
    • Proteolytic activation.
  • In proteolytic activation, the inactive form of the enzyme (called a zymogen or proenzyme) is cleaved at one or several locations (peptide bonds) irreversibly and permanently, thereby transforming the enzyme into its active form.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 90-92

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: The first step of glucose metabolism requires either glucokinase or hexokinase I, which are isozymes. Which of the following about these isozymes is NOT true:

options.label: B
options.text: Hexokinase is found in all cells

questions.solutionHtml:
Hexokinase is specific for glucose

Hexokinase is a general enzyme that can phosphorylate any hexose sugar. It is not specific to glucose.

PROPERTIES OF TWO ISOENZYMES OF HEXOKINASE

Hexokinase

Glucokinase (Hexokinase IV)

●        Phosphorylates all hexoses

●        Phosphorylates only Glucose

●        Present in all cells

●        Present in the liver and pancreas (GLUT-2)

●        High affinity

●        less substrate required

●        active in the fasting state

●        low km

●        low Vmax

●        Low affinity,

●        more substrate required

●        active in the fed state

●        high km

●        high Vmax

●        Feedback inhibition by Glucose-6-Phosphate

●        Induced by Insulin




Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page no. 164-166

questions.topic: eGurukul · Enzyme Regulation & Uses of Enzymes
questions.stem: A patient presented with yellowish eyes and skin, itching, pain in the upper right side of the abdomen, and weight loss. Laboratory analysis of urine bilirubin indicated obstructive jaundice. The test of which of the following enzyme will substantiate these findings?
questions.solutionHtml:
ALP
  • ALP (Alkaline Phosphatase) catalyzes the removal of the phosphate group from organic phosphate esters at alkaline pH.
  • There are 4 isoenzymes for the ALP enzyme
  1. ALP-I → Intestinal
  • ALP-L→ tissue non-specific present mainly in the Liver, bone, and kidneys
  • ALP-P→ Placental isoenzyme is also called Regan isoenzyme and is increased during pregnancy.
  • GC type (Germ cell type) → Present in Germ cell
  • It is widely distributed in different cells and organs of the body but is most useful to mark any bone and liver pathology.
  • It is raised moderately in hepatocellular damage and very high levels of ALP is seen in obstructive jaundice and is considered one of the best enzyme biomarkers for biliary obstruction
  • It is also raised in bone diseases such as Paget disease, rickets, osteomalacia, hyperparathyroidism
  • Decreased ALP is seen in hypothyroidism and in women taking OCPs and estrogen therapy.



Lippincott Illustrated Reviews Biochemistry. 7th edition Page no. 250
